title: chore: replace Babel with esbuild
description:
Babel earns its keep in exactly two places in this repo, neither of which touches production code: `babel-jest` transforms a handful of ESM-only `node_modules` for unit tests, and `@babel/cli` transpiles three of them to CommonJS so the CJS integration tests can `require()` them. `esbuild`, which already builds the whole extension, does both jobs — so this MR removes `@babel/cli`, `@babel/core` and `@babel/preset-env` and deletes `babel.config.js`. The lockfile loses **99 packages** and **no new dependency is added** (`esbuild` and `glob` were already devDependencies).

The trigger was https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-vscode-extension/-/merge_requests/3259+, the Renovate MR bumping `@babel/preset-env` to v8. Making that one green needed a `@babel/core` v8 bump, a `ts-jest` peer dependency `override`, a `babel.config.js` change (Babel 8 no longer transforms ES modules to CommonJS by default), and a ~4.5k-line lockfile diff — all to keep a dev-only tool alive. Removing Babel instead makes that MR, and every future Babel MR, unnecessary.

## What changed

- **`jest_esm_transformer.js` (new)** — a 15-line Jest transformer calling `esbuild.transformSync({ format: 'cjs' })`, following the existing `jest_html_transformer.js` pattern. `jest.config.js` points the ESM `node_modules` pattern at it instead of `babel-jest`.
- **`scripts/transpile_es_to_cjs_for_integration_tests.mjs`** — the `babel` CLI call is replaced by a per-file `esbuild.transform` that keeps the directory layout. Per-file rather than bundling, because these packages have relative imports between files and deep entry points (e.g. `uuid/dist/esm/*`) that the integration test workspace resolves directly.
- **`package.json` / `package-lock.json`** — the three `@babel/*` devDependencies are gone; 2281 → 2182 lockfile packages.
- **`.eslintrc.json`** — allow devDependency imports from `jest_*.js`, same as the existing allowance for `scripts/**`.

`@babel/*` still appears in the lockfile transitively, via `jest` (`babel-jest`, `babel-plugin-istanbul`) and `@sentry/vite-plugin`. Those are not ours to remove. `webviews/vue2` keeps its own Babel setup and is untouched.

## How has this been tested

All of the following were run locally on this branch:

- `npm run test:unit` — 293 suites, 2518 tests pass. (One suite intermittently reports `FAIL` with zero failing tests, the pre-existing "worker process failed to exit gracefully" flake; it passes when run alone.)
- `npm run build:desktop` — succeeds.
- `npm run build:transpile-es-to-cjs-for-integration-tests` — succeeds, and the output is genuinely CommonJS: `rg "^export |^import "` over `dist-desktop/node_modules/{nanoevents,@anycable/core,uuid}` finds nothing, and I `require()`d each transpiled package from Node and called into it.
- `npm run test:integration` — ran against the real VS Code 1.92.2: 61 passing, 1 pending, exit 0.
- `npm run lint` and `prettier --check` — no errors on the touched files.
- Lockfile validity — `npm ci --ignore-scripts` from a clean directory with both npm 10.9.2 (the npm bundled with the node 22.14.0 we pin in `.tool-versions` and use in CI) and npm 11.

<details>
<summary>Lockfile diff audit</summary>

I diffed the `.packages` key sets of the old and new lockfile rather than eyeballing 2.6k lines:

- 99 entries removed, 0 added
- every removed entry is Babel-only: `@babel/*`, `regexpu-core`, `unicode-*`, `regenerate*`, `regjs*`, the `browserslist`/`caniuse-lite`/`electron-to-chromium`/`node-releases` data packages, plus `@babel/cli`'s `@nicolo-ribaudo/chokidar-2`, `fs-readdir-recursive` and `lodash.debounce`
- no non-Babel package changed version

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why esbuild and not @swc/jest</summary>

`@swc/jest` would work too, but `esbuild` is already a direct devDependency and already the build tool for the extension, the browser build and the integration-test transpile. Using it keeps the toolchain to one transpiler and adds nothing to the dependency tree.

</details>
